name: Ace OP16 + 4x OP16-015 (setBasePower live-play probe)
note: NOT a tuned list. Purpose-built to play the setBasePower primitive inside runBotMatch, which no test did: all 28 of its unit tests are OnePieceTestEngine fixtures. That is the gap the OP16-118 search-to-hand defect fell through -- it passed unit tests and aborted live games with illegal-command. OP16-015's clause is the risky shape: an optional block with a trashFromHand cost carrying two filters, resolving into TWO setBasePower actions, one of which auto-resolves a single-candidate leader target. Derived from ace-op16.json by swapping the 4 OP05-019 slots, which are Block 1 and rotated out anyway. Leader is OP16-001 Ace, which is also what OP16-015's parked cost-reduction clause keys on.
